title: Beyond the 956: Stacy Keach, TV's Mike Hammer, dies at 85
excerpt: Stacy Keach, the veteran actor best known as television's Mike Hammer and narrator of CNBC's American Greed, has died at 85. He died November 10, 2026, at his family home in Poland after a long battle with heart failure.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Stacy Keach, the veteran actor best known as television's Mike Hammer and as the narrator of CNBC's American Greed, has died at 85.

Keach died Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at his family home in Magdalenka, Poland, after a long battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure, his wife, Malgosia Tomassi Keach, announced. The Hollywood Reporter published his obituary on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.

Keach was born Walter Stacy Keach Jr. on June 2, 1941, in Savannah, Georgia. He first made his name on the stage, where he was regarded as one of the finest American Shakespearean actors of his era, playing Hamlet, Richard III, King Lear, Falstaff, and Macbeth, and earning a Tony Award nomination for his performance in Arthur Kopit's Indians in 1969. He was inducted into the Theatre Hall of Fame and received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2019.

On film, he won acclaim as the washed-up boxer Billy Tully in John Huston's Fat City (1972), and appeared in The New Centurions (1972), Doc (1971), The Life and Times of Judge Roy Bean (1972), The Ninth Configuration (1980), The Long Riders (1980), American History X (1998), The Bourne Legacy (2012), and Nebraska (2013). He played Sgt. Stedenko in Cheech & Chong's Up in Smoke (1978) and Nice Dreams (1981), and voiced Skipper in Disney's Planes (2013).

Television audiences knew him best as Mickey Spillane's private detective Mike Hammer, a role he played in the 1983 telefilm Murder Me, Murder You, the CBS series Mickey Spillane's Mike Hammer (1984-1987), and the syndicated Mike Hammer, Private Eye (1997-1998). He played Ken Titus on the Fox sitcom Titus (2000-2002), Warden Henry Pope on Prison Break, and Matt LeBlanc's father on Man with a Plan. He won a Golden Globe and was nominated for an Emmy for playing Ernest Hemingway in the 1988 miniseries Hemingway. For nearly two decades, his voice guided viewers through CNBC's true-crime series American Greed.

Keach is survived by his wife, Malgosia Tomassi Keach.

Rest in Peace, Stacy Keach.

Sources: The Hollywood Reporter (obituary by Mike Barnes, November 10, 2026); Wikipedia.
